findings.reason: The original flagged 1200×1400 PNG, independently viewed standalone at original resolution, visibly prints max_{||v||=1} ||Tv|| in the operator-norm reference in F3 and again F5. The frozen consumer contains an unaliased wikilink, so this historical defect came from the primary supplier title. The genuine la_004 immutable adjudication records its title-only repair, and the current supplier title contains inline math. A fresh current native reference-map preview of this unchanged consumer visibly typesets the maximum subscript and both norms in both references; both generated anchor contents contain KaTeX. Thus the historical defect is confirmed and currently resolved upstream.

source_lines_after.53: [F3] On a nonzero domain the operator norm is defined by its maximum on unit vectors; on the zero domain it is zero. It is submultiplicative ([[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]], [[cor-operator-norm-submultiplicative-and-t-star-t-identity]]).
source_lines_after.57: [F5] For a finite-dimensional map $A$, $\|A\|=\|A^*\|$: Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|A\|=\max_{\|x\|=\|y\|=1}|\langle Ax,y\rangle|$ when both spaces are nonzero (choose $y=Ax/\|Ax\|$ when $Ax\ne0$), and the adjoint identity exchanges $x,y$; if a space is zero both map norms are zero ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]).
